sections.markdown:
## C — School bus exceptions on multi-lane roads, parking rules and procedures, hill parking, changing lanes, entering and exiting highways, and passing safely
Knowledge domain: when a South Carolina driver may keep going past a stopped school bus and when they must wait, where and how to park including disability spaces and hills, how to change lanes, join and leave a highway, and how to pass or be passed safely; the zipper merge facts continue in part C2.

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
If you meet a stopped school bus while heading the other way on a multi-lane highway or a multi-lane private road, you are not required to stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
For this rule, a multi-lane highway or private road is one with four lanes, having at least two traffic lanes in each direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
On any highway you must always stop when you are behind a stopped school bus. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Once stopped for a school bus, you may not move on until the bus moves or its red lights stop flashing, under SC Code §56-5-2760. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
When you park, you are responsible for making sure your vehicle does not obstruct anyone. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
A vehicle with a disability license plate or placard may use designated disability spaces only when it is driven by, or carrying, the person whose name is on the plate or placard registration. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A02
When parking along a roadway, keep your vehicle no more than 18 inches from the curb or the edge of the pavement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A02
Parking is banned in many areas, so look for signs or painted curbs that prohibit or limit it, since some restrictions are shown by colored curb markings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A02
To enter a perpendicular or angle parking space, pick out the space, check traffic and signal your intention. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A02
Move forward slowly, turning the wheel left or right as needed until the vehicle reaches the middle of the space, then center it there. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A02
To leave a perpendicular or angle space, check traffic in every direction and keep checking while you back straight out until your front bumper clears the vehicle beside you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A03
Then turn the wheel sharply toward where the rear should go, and once you are clear of the space, stop, shift to drive and accelerate smoothly while straightening the wheels. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A03
To parallel park, first pick out the space, check traffic and signal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A03
When traffic is clear, shift into reverse and look toward the rear in the direction the vehicle will travel. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A03
Back slowly while turning the wheel quickly in the correct direction, and keep backing until your front bumper lines up with the rear bumper of the vehicle you are parking behind. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A03
Keep backing slowly while turning the wheel quickly to bring the vehicle into the center of the space. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A03
Stop before your bumper touches the vehicle behind, shift to drive to adjust your position, and finish no more than 18 inches from the curb or pavement edge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A04
To leave a parallel space, check traffic all around, hold the brake, shift to reverse and back up as close as you can to the vehicle parked behind. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A04
Next signal, check traffic with your mirrors and over your shoulder, shift to drive and pull forward slowly while steering into the lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A04
Move into the traffic lane once your door has passed the rear bumper of the vehicle parked ahead of you. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A04
When parking headed downhill, with or without a curb, turn the wheels to the right, except when you park on the left side of a one-way street. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A04
When parking headed uphill next to a curb, turn the wheels toward the center of the street so the back of the front tire rests against the curb. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A04
When parking headed uphill with no curb, turn the wheels to the right so the vehicle would roll off the road if the brakes failed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A04
In every hill-parking case, set the parking brake, put the vehicle in park or the proper gear and turn the engine off, using first or reverse in a manual transmission. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A05
The hill parking figure sums up the rules: downhill, wheels toward the curb; uphill with a curb, wheels away from it; uphill without a curb, wheels to the right. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A05
To change lanes, check your mirrors, then check your blind spots by turning your head and looking over your shoulder toward the side you plan to move to. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A05
Then find a gap in traffic, signal, look again toward the new lane, adjust your speed and steer in. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A05
When entering a multi-lane highway, use the acceleration lane, which runs alongside the main roadway, to reach the speed of other traffic before you pull on. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A05
Find a gap, merge into the traffic flow and then cancel your turn signal. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A06
Know where you will leave the roadway, and move early to the lane closest to your exit so you do not need a sudden lane change. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A06
Hold your speed while you are still on the main roadway, then signal, move into the deceleration lane, check the posted speed and adjust to it. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A06
On multi-lane roads, the left-most lane is the one used for passing slower vehicles. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A06
Never pass on the shoulder, paved or not, because the shoulder is a hard surface on the right meant as an emergency stopping lane, not for through traffic. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A06
Pass as quickly and safely as you can, since the longer you ride alongside another vehicle, the longer you risk sitting in its blind spot as it moves toward your lane. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A06
Before passing, check for oncoming traffic and check your mirrors and over your shoulder for vehicles following or passing you. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec10-F36 | anchor: A07
When it is safe to pass, signal your intention at least 100 feet before you pass. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F37 | anchor: A07
Keep passing until the entire front of the passed vehicle shows in your rearview mirror, then signal, check over your shoulder and steer smoothly back into the lane. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F38 | anchor: A07
When someone is passing you, stay in your lane, hold a steady speed so they can get by, and stay alert to protect yourself from unsafe moves by others. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F39 | anchor: A07
Do not try to pass when an oncoming vehicle is approaching, when a curve or hill blocks your view, at intersections, or before a highway-railroad crossing or a bridge. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F40 | anchor: A07
When passing a bicyclist, slow down, leave as much space as possible and take the bicyclist's speed into account. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0090]

Misconceptions: a driver behind a stopped school bus must always stop, even on a multi-lane highway, and only opposite-direction drivers on a multi-lane road may continue; a disability placard alone does not allow use of a disability space unless the named person is driving or riding; the shoulder is never a passing lane, even when paved; when being passed you keep a steady speed rather than speeding up; uphill beside a curb is the one hill case where the wheels turn away from the curb.
Mnemonics: downhill or uphill with no curb, wheels to the right; uphill with a curb, wheels to the street's center; eighteen inches is the farthest you may park from the curb; signal at least one hundred feet before you pass; pass until the whole front of the other car shows in your rearview mirror.
Glossary: multi-lane highway means, for the school bus rule, a road of four lanes with at least two in each direction; acceleration lane means the lane alongside the main roadway used to reach traffic speed; deceleration lane means the lane to the right of the roadway, before the ramp, used to slow down; shoulder means the hard surface on the right kept for emergency stops; placard means the disability parking permit displayed in a vehicle.

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
